question: Why did Andrej Karpathy build his own video site instead of using YouTube's recommendations?

rungs.question: Why did Karpathy build HackerTube?
rungs.answer: The one source read says he was frustrated with the videos YouTube suggested to him, so he built his own alternative.

evidence.quote: Andrej Karpathy was frustrated with YouTube’s video suggestions, so he used Claude to build his own alternative in just two hours.

counter.text: None found. Scope: the one Instagram post. It credits 'Andrej Karpathy / X' but links no post, so his own words were not read and only one site carries the claim.

rungs.question: Why could one person build a working video site in about two hours?
rungs.answer: The post says an AI model, Claude Opus 5.5, did almost all of it: writing the code, securing the site and launching it. Karpathy only set up an API key, arranged a server and bought a domain.

evidence.quote: Karpathy used Claude Opus 5.5 to handle almost everything, from writing code to securing and launching the site.
He only stepped in to set up an API key, arrange a server, and buy a domain.

counter.text: None found. Scope: the one Instagram post; the two-hour figure and the split of work are reported second hand and not checked against Karpathy's own account.

rungs.question: Why would its picks differ from what YouTube's algorithm suggests?
rungs.answer: The videos come from people, not a ranking system: 6,454 videos drawn from 43 million Hacker News comments over 20 years, so each pick was once mentioned by a real commenter.

evidence.quote: Called HackerTube, the website features 6,454 videos picked from 43 million Hacker News comments spanning 20 years.
lets users discover videos recommended by real people instead of YouTube’s algorithm.

counter.text: The 43 million figure is all Hacker News comments in the period, not 43 million recommendations; the post does not say how many comments actually named a video. Scope: the one Instagram post.

rungs.question: Why were these 6,454 videos chosen out of everything mentioned in those comments?
rungs.answer: Nothing read answers this. The post does not say how a mention became a pick, whether by count, score or another rule.

counter.text: none found; scope: the one Instagram post, which gives no selection method

landing.shows: On the one secondary source read, the story is about who does the recommending: an AI model did nearly all the building, and the site swaps YouTube's ranking for videos Hacker News commenters mentioned. How mentions were turned into 6,454 picks is not in what was read, and Karpathy's own post was not linked.
landing.open_question: If a list built from what people actually told each other can be made in an afternoon, what is a recommendation algorithm still doing for you?
